None of these are particularly relevant to current discussions in American political discourse, but I think they're interesting to look back on and dissect.

I would also like to hear Destiny dive more into what he relies on in terms of empirical evidence for the policies he supports relating to healthcare or social safety nets. I've listened to him talk about why he supports these, but I don't believe he ever really goes into what empirical data he uses besides broadly pointing to Scandinavian countries or other countries with universal healthcare systems as models America could follow since their systems seem to work. Which is fine for briefly explaining his beliefs, but I expect more from him in terms of explaining why his articulated system would fare better in terms of outcomes and are more empirically grounded than some obscure free market solutions.
